name: United Arab Republic (Egypt)

areaKm2.note: Official area 1,001,450 km2 incl. Sinai; hb:1960 Egypt polygon computes to ~1,000,600 km2 on the sphere. Gaza Strip (Egyptian-administered) excluded.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1967 = 30,892k (mid). Low: 1966 census 30.08M grown 2%. High: OWID/UN 32,196,366 and World Bank 1967 (32.2M).

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share 1967 = 42.3%; 1966 census urban share ~40% (low).

activePersonnel.note: COW NMC v7 milper 1967 = 220,000 (mid). CIA memo 26 June 1967: ground forces ~217,000 incl. 35,000 in Yemen; CIA/DIA table 26 May: ground forces 175,000 before mobilisation. Plus air force and navy ~25,000 -> 200,000-242,000. Pollack 2004 p. 59 via Six-Day War article: 160,000 total, 100,000 in Sinai.

trainedReserves.note: Reservists called up in May 1967. CIA/DIA 26 May: ground forces 175,000 before mobilisation, 200,000 at M+15 (+25,000, low) and "limited reserves at home". High allows the wider reserve call-up reported in May 1967. Grade C.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 220,000 minus P roles ~92,000: air force (~20,000), navy (~11,000), armour, artillery, air-defence, logistics and staff. Grade C.

mobilizationRatio.note: Egypt fielded ~0.65-0.85M in 1973 (Yom Kippur War infobox) from ~35M people = 1.9-2.4%; a total-war ceiling of 4-8% is assumed given limited conscript training capacity. Grade C.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Infantry of 9 divisions and 28 independent brigades (CIA 26 June 1967; ground forces 217,000), incl. ~35,000 troops in Yemen. Infantry share ~40% of ground forces. Reconstruction, grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Soviet small arms (AK, SKS) and RPG-2, little night equipment.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: conscripts, poor flexibility and improvisation (CIA 26 May 1967); reservists barely trained (Pollack ch. 1).

count.note: Educated guess: Sa'iqa commandos and paratroop battalions (two commando battalions flown to Jordan in June 1967).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: volunteer commandos with Yemen experience.

count.note: Six-Day War article (Pollack 2004 p. 59): 1,000 artillery pieces in Sinai; plus guns west of the canal and in Yemen. CIA/DIA table also lists 200 SP antitank/assault guns (SU-100).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Soviet 122 mm and 130 mm guns, outranging Israeli artillery.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: rigid pre-planned fire, weak observation.

count.note: CIA memo 26 June 1967: ~1,000 tanks before the war (350 T-34, 400 T-54, 123 T-55, plus IS-3, PT-76, Centurion and Sherman); CIA/DIA table 26 May: 1,007. Pollack 2004 p. 59: 900-950 in Sinai.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: T-54/55 era-typical, but over a third were WWII T-34/85.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: poor gunnery and maintenance; ~500 tanks lost in Sinai (CIA June 1967).

count.note: Six-Day War article (Pollack 2004 p. 59): 1,100 APCs in Sinai; total incl. units west of the canal and Yemen somewhat higher. BTR-152, BTR-40, Walid.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: wheeled open-topped BTR-152.

count.note: CIA/DIA memo 26 May 1967: 239 operationally assigned jet fighters, primarily MiG-17 and MiG-21. ~300 of ~430 combat aircraft were destroyed, mostly on the ground (CIA 26 June).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: MiG-21F-13/PF Mach 2 interceptors; MiG-17 obsolescent.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: low sortie rates, no hardened shelters, caught on the ground in Operation Focus.

count.note: CIA 26 June 1967: ~430 available combat aircraft before hostilities; CIA/DIA 26 May: 70 operational jet bombers (Tu-16, Il-28). 430 - 239 fighters = ~190 incl. Su-7 fighter-bombers and MiG-15/17 ground-attack (high).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Tu-16 with AS-1 cruise missiles, Il-28 obsolescent.

count.note: Educated guess: Mi-4 and Mi-6 transport helicopters, used extensively in Yemen.
CIA/DIA 26 May 1967: six destroyers (Skoryy class, ex-RN Z-class El Nasser/El Fateh); high adds 2-3 frigates and escort vessels.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: 1950s Soviet destroyers.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: CIA rates Egyptian ships ~80% as effective as Israeli due to poor maintenance and sea time.

count.note: CIA/DIA 26 May 1967: 18 missile patrol boats (Osa, Komar) (low); plus torpedo boats, submarine chasers and minesweepers (~20-40). Grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Styx-armed Komar sank INS Eilat in October 1967, the first anti-ship missile kill (Egyptian Navy article).

count.note: CIA/DIA 26 May 1967: 12 submarines (Soviet W and R class).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Whiskey/Romeo diesel boats.

count.note: Educated guess: SA-2 battalions defending the Suez Canal and Cairo areas (CIA 26 May 1967: of limited effectiveness; few AAA defences on the four Sinai fighter bases); count not given in the fetched sources.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: SA-2 high-altitude SAM, useless against low-level attack.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25. Evidence: Amer's politicised command, contradictory deployment orders in May 1967, general withdrawal order of 6 June collapsed the Sinai army (Pollack, Arabs at War ch. 1).

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.25-0.5. Evidence: national conscript army but deep officer-soldier divide; units disintegrated in the retreat.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5. Evidence: high pre-war public confidence, but 35,000 men tied down in Yemen; collapsed after 6 June.

weapons.note: Anchor: between 8 (1943) and 9 (1985). Evidence: SA-2 SAMs, Styx anti-ship missiles, Mach 2 MiG-21; no ATGMs.

armor.note: Anchor: 8 = RHA. Evidence: T-54/55 steel armour, a third still T-34.

ships.note: Anchor: 8 = radar, submarines. Evidence: Osa/Komar missile boats, 12 submarines, WWII-era destroyers.

fortification.note: Anchor: 8. Evidence: Soviet-style layered field defences at Abu Ageila and Rafah; no hardened aircraft shelters.

logistics.note: Anchor: 8 = motor transport. Evidence: motorised supply, but sustained 60,000 men in Yemen (CIA 26 May 1967).

communications.note: Anchor: 8 = company radio. Evidence: Soviet radio sets, but centralised, slow reporting.

isr.note: Anchor: 8 = radar. Evidence: early-warning radar network (blind at low level); no satellites.

air.note: Anchor: air 8 = 1943, 9 = 1985. Evidence: MiG-21, Su-7, Tu-16 jets.

cyber.note: No military computer-network capability before ~1985 (cyber anchor 9 = 1990 networks).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV): Egypt 1967 = 1,835 (2011 int$). Range +/-10%.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

industrialShare.note: World Bank NV.IND.TOTL.ZS: industry (incl. construction) 23.8% of GDP in 1967.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) Egypt 1967 = 53.7% (1989 Apr vintage 53.8%). Egypt was a wheat importer; that does not lower this value. Share 53.7% (range 50.0-57.0%) -> 0.463 (0.43-0.5).

annualCohort.note: World Bank SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y and SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN (https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ISR;EGY/indicator/SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y?date=1967:1973&format=json): 16,144,385 x 10.23% / 5 = ~330,300 males per year; only men were conscripted. audit 2026-10-30: males only, the conscript-pool convention of all other snapshots (derived:cohort-from-agegroup applied to the male term only); was 645,700 for both sexes.

artillery.note: Educated guess: Factory 99 etc. produced mortars, ammunition and small arms; guns came from the USSR.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess: Helwan HA-300 programme abandoned 1969; licence assembly of trainers only.

missiles.note: Educated guess: al-Zafir/al-Kahir rockets under development with German engineers; CIA: not deployed.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: paved roads of the Nile valley and delta plus coastal and canal roads; Sinai mostly tracks.

railKm.note: Educated guess: Egyptian National Railways ~4,500-4,800 km incl. the El Qantara-El Arish line.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Alexandria, Port Said, Suez, Safaga.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: small national merchant fleet (~200-300k GRT) x 1.5.

supplyRangeKm.note: CIA 26 May 1967: Egypt fed and armed up to 60,000 men in Yemen at the end of a thousand-mile supply line (sea route; high). Overland in Sinai ~200-250 km from the canal (mid). Grade C.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: buffaloes, cattle, donkeys and camels on Egyptian farms; negligible military use.

homeDefense.note: 1.1 row: familiar terrain and local supply in Sinai; the Nile valley behind the canal adds fortified cities and population support (1.2).

notes: Snapshot date 5 June 1967. Official name United Arab Republic (Egypt), kept after Syria left the union in 1961. Territory: hb:1960:Egypt incl. Sinai; the Egyptian-administered Gaza Strip is excluded. Personnel: activePersonnel = standing conscript and regular forces incl. ~35,000 in Yemen (listed as a base abroad), trainedReserves = reservists called up in May 1967. Key sources: CIA/DIA memo "Military Capabilities of Israel and the Arab States" 26 May 1967 (UAR: 175,000 ground forces before mobilisation, 1,007 tanks, 200 SP guns, 239 jet fighters, 70 jet bombers, 6 destroyers, 12 submarines, 18 missile boats); CIA memo of 26 June 1967 on Soviet resupply (217,000 ground forces, ~1,000 tanks, ~430 combat aircraft before the war); Six-Day War article quoting Pollack, Arabs at War p. 59. IISS Military Balance 1967-68 not fetched (paywalled). Weakest: air-defence battery count, reserves, helicopter count.
